text: History before the seal. Both constants (DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_INITIAL_READ_TIMEOUT_MS = 300, DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_CONTROLLER_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 300) were introduced by 9939b3ff6 (2026-02-24, 'node orchestration hardening') and never changed; src/config/dynamic-config-startup-wiring.js was last touched by 54dd2d7ce (2026-10-27), 8a2bd2b44, 06273547c and b1acc899f, none changing the bounds or their fallback. The bounded-wait census of 2026-10-04 (solve/epics/raft-rs-full-cutover/census-bounded-waits-2026-10-04.md lines 114 and 442-443) classified both as startup time-boxes with a designed fallback, 'Defaults apply now and CDC applies the stored values later', fallthrough_alternative, warn, and test/config/dynamic-config-startup-wait-bound-spent.test.js witnesses that classification (an expired box logs INITIAL_APPLY_FAILED, never wait_bound_spent, and startup proceeds). No other quest names dynamic-config startup (grep of solve/quests and solve/epics: only the two censuses, the f1-step-down-port static investigation and the system-table-write-admission design mention the wiring). New evidence against the designed fallback: the wiring applies a late value only through handleCdcApplied on CDC_APPLIED events for the config table (dynamic-config-startup-wiring.js 451-477), so a stored value already local with no later CDC apply (a restarting node) is never applied; and the spent controller bound orphans a live RaftAdaptiveTimingController (withTimeout 76-107 never cancels; the reference is dropped 438-449; initialize, registerWatchers and startLoop continue; shutdown 492-501 shuts only the controller held). The seal supersedes the 2026-10-04 classification explicitly (R09) and requires the witness test to be re-derived, not deleted (ruling of the lead).

seal.statement: src/config/dynamic-config-startup-wiring.js is the one owner of the node's startup dynamic configuration, rows 4 and 5 of the fixed-work-bound census (the same wiring owns both, so they are one quest). When the 300 ms startup bound DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_INITIAL_READ_TIMEOUT_MS is spent, the late value of that key is still applied, by the same owner, whether it arrives by the completed read or by a CDC apply of the config table: a stored value already local with no later CDC apply (a restarting node) is applied when its read completes, never silently left at the default. When DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_CONTROLLER_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS is spent, the in-flight RaftAdaptiveTimingController.initialize() is never orphaned: the controller either becomes owned when it completes (then shut down by the wiring's shutdown) or is cancelled and shut down, never both, never a second controller beside it, with a typed startup outcome recorded either way. Under R09 this supersedes, explicitly, the designed-fallback classification of both 300 ms boxes recorded by the bounded-wait census of 2026-10-04 (solve/epics/raft-rs-full-cutover/census-bounded-waits-2026-10-04.md lines 114, 442-443: 'Defaults apply now and CDC applies the stored values later') and witnessed by test/config/dynamic-config-startup-wait-bound-spent.test.js: new evidence shows the late value is applied only through handleCdcApplied on CDC_APPLIED events for the config table (dynamic-config-startup-wiring.js 451-477), so a value with no later CDC apply is never applied, and the spent controller bound orphans a live controller (withTimeout 76-107 never cancels; the wiring drops its reference 438-449; initialize, registerWatchers and the loop continue; shutdown 492-501 only shuts the controller it holds). That witness test is re-derived to the new contract, never deleted. Startup still never blocks on the bounds.

text: Red first, before any src change: test/config/dynamic-config-startup-owned-initialization.test.js (config reads that answer only after 700 ms, longer than the 300 ms read bound and the controller's own 300 ms bound, which starts after the reads). Row 4: a restarting node's stored raft timing (heartbeat 120, election 1800-5400, tick 25), no CDC apply: the replicas end on the defaults (heartbeat 50), never the stored values (not ok at the behavioural same()). Row 5: raft.adaptiveTimingEnabled stored true: the orphaned controller's initialize completes after the bound and starts its loop; after wiring.shutdown() its interval is still alive (not ok at intervals.live.size === 0). The existing witnesses stay green at the base: dynamic-config-startup-wiring.test.js 38 assertions, dynamic-config-startup-wait-bound-spent.test.js 25 (evidence/red-before-fix.log.txt).
